resources.string: Choose Hex Preview in the list
Allow the microphone in Hex Preview

Hex turns speech into text on this phone and never uploads your voice or what you type with its keyboard. It keeps no keystrokes or transcripts. Two labs keep what they learn on this phone, and only once you turn them on: Learn from my fixes keeps the word pairs you corrected after dictating, and Adaptive touch keeps an average of where you tap each key. Delete what Hex learned in Labs removes both. Pick the English model for this phone, once you turn it on, keeps only how long your recent dictations took to transcribe against how long you spoke, and a few counts, never words or audio; turning it off deletes them. Clipboard history in Labs, only once you turn it on, reads what you copy and keeps the last 20 texts on this phone, each for an hour unless you pin it. It skips text an app marks as sensitive and anything copied while a password field is open, and turning it off deletes them. Feedback leaves the phone only when you tap Send in Send feedback: then your message, the pictures you keep, your email if you add one and details about Hex and this phone go to Anomaly’s feedback inbox (Bellhop). Your dictations, recordings, vocabulary and corrections are never included. To find updates, Hex Preview asks GitHub for its latest version when you open it and at most once a day from the keyboard. That request carries nothing about you or what you type, though GitHub sees your internet address, as with any website. Turn it off with Check for updates automatically.

Your browser downloads it from GitHub. Open the download and tap Update when Android asks. The first time, Android asks you to allow your browser to install apps. Allow it, go back, and tap the download again.
Updating closes the keyboard for a moment. Tap a text field to bring it back.
